summary: GB300 NVL72 drawing 132 kW at the rack; the liquid loop and CDU, not the GPU, are the 2026 bottleneck.
full_text: Primary checks: GB300 NVL72 configurations are quoting 120–132 kW at the rack wall. GPU silicon is not the constraint — facility CDU capacity, rear-door vs direct-to-chip mix, and 415V busway are. Several US colos still cannot deliver >80 kW/rack without a 9–12 month electrical upgrade. This is a site-selection and power-contract story before it is a chip story.

summary: CoWoS-L still ~20% short of 2026 GPU-pack demand; N2 risked wafers now quoted in the high-teens $k.
full_text: Foundry checks: CoWoS-L allocated capacity for 2026 remains roughly 20% below GPU-pack ask after the latest customer forecast lock. CoWoS-R is filling the overflow, with worse yields on the largest interposers. N2 risked wafers are being quoted in the high-teens thousands of dollars; that is a mix/ASP print, not a unit-volume print. Substrate and OSAT, not litho, are the secondary bottleneck.

summary: Custom XPU backlog now the second AI silicon print; merchant GPU mix is no longer the whole tape-out story.
full_text: Three hyperscalers have locked 2026–27 custom XPU revisions with the same networking-silicon vendor that already owns the switch ASIC socket. This is not a one-off Google TPU analogue — it is a multi-year, multi-die, CoWoS-consuming backlog. Merchant GPU still takes the majority of advanced packaging, but the incremental 2027 wafer is increasingly custom. Attach for SerDes, HBM PHY and CPO is the second-order read.

summary: MI350 rack qualification still lagging on memory map and scale-out NIC; software stack, not FLOPs, is the gate.
full_text: MI350/MI355 qualification at two US hyperscalers is still gated on the memory map and the scale-out NIC firmware, not peak FLOPs. ROCm 7 closed a set of kernel gaps but collective performance at 256+ GPU domains remains the diligence item. A 2026 merchant-GPU share gain is possible; it is not in the bag on silicon photographs. Watch the NIC and the compiler before the die shot.

summary: HBM4 bits/wafer are not the 2026 bottleneck; substrate, OSAT and HBF attach are.
full_text: HBM3E remains sold-out through 1H26 on the leading stack. HBM4 samples are in customer labs; bits/wafer look fine. The constraint is the base-die, the substrate and the OSAT line that actually stacks them. One US memory vendor is quoting 2026 HBM revenue as >50% of DRAM. That is a mix story with gross-margin torque, not a bit-growth story. Chart: vendor supply vs packaging-limited demand.

summary: 1.6T SerDes taping out with three switch/XPU houses; reach at 224G is the diligence, not the press slide.
full_text: 224G SerDes IP is in three simultaneous 1.6T switch/XPU tape-outs. The question is reach over the backplane and the retimer count, not whether the SerDes exists. AEL/AEC copper still takes the in-rack hop; optics take the longer hop. That mix, not a single transceiver TAM slide, sets 2026–27 content per rack. Watch retimer attach and the LPO vs DSP split.

summary: 51.2T leaf/spine is shipping into GB200 halls; the 2026 print is optics and power, not the switch ASIC.
full_text: 51.2T leaf/spine is no longer a lab item — it is landing in GB200/GB300 halls. The switch ASIC is not the scarce part. 800G/1.6T optics, liquid manifolds and the SONiC image that actually stays up are. One US networking vendor is taking the majority of those leaves in the current build cycle. Ethernet vs proprietary scale-up remains a 2027 debate; Ethernet already won scale-out.

summary: Pay-per-crawl via HTTP 402 is live as merchant-of-record; this is a toll booth on agent web access, not a CDN footnote.
full_text: HTTP 402 pay-per-crawl is in production as merchant of record on agent fetches. Workers remains a real sandbox spoke for agent code; the network is the path agents take to the public web. That is occupancy of more than one spoke at once. Cache, bot management and the crawl toll are the 2026 revenue tells — not a seat count. Institutional protection is still near-zero; occupancy is the thesis.

summary: CyberArk close shifts the 2026 print to identity attach on the platform, not the multiple paid.
full_text: CyberArk is closed. The 2026 question is platform attach of privileged identity onto the installed firewall/SASE base, not the acquisition multiple. Secrets brokering is a real callable surface for agents; CVE dashboards are not. Watch identity ARR mix, remaining-performance-obligation disclosure, and whether PANW sales motion actually pulls CyberArk into the core platform deal or leaves it as a bolt-on.

summary: Charlotte AI is the vendor wielding intelligence; the endpoint agent still is not a spoke the orchestrator must call.
full_text: Charlotte and the rest of the 'agentic SOC' wave are the vendor using intelligence. Under an AGI-now frame that is not occupancy. The Falcon sensor remains in the telemetry path — a 4, not a 6. What would change the score is an identity/entitlement primitive the orchestrator cannot route around. Watch module attach and net-new ARR, not demo videos. Identity names still screen cleaner on P1.

summary: OCI training clusters are being sold against the same power-constrained US sites as everyone else; contract duration is the tell.
full_text: OCI is signing multi-year training-cluster deals into the same constrained US power markets as the other three. The differentiator is remaining unused capacity on existing campuses plus the database/SaaS gravity that keeps inference on-OCI after training. Stargate-class headlines are not the print. Remaining performance obligation, GPU-hour utilisation and whether the customer brings the model or the data are.

summary: Atlas Vector Search is in the write-path for two production agent apps; that is occupancy of the document store, not a feature launch.
full_text: Two production agent applications are writing tool-call traces and retrieving chunks through Atlas Vector Search on the same cluster that holds the operational documents. That is a spoke: agents both retrieve from and write to it. Consumption billing converts that traffic. The risk is the vector store is one of several equivalents — occupancy is real, default status is not yet. Watch Atlas RPO mix vs enterprise server.

summary: An agent making a credit decision still has to request a score it cannot compute; that is a callable API with no substitute.
full_text: FICO remains the only vertical name with a clean P1-6: an agent taking a credit action must request a score it is not allowed to invent. Per-inquiry royalties scale with origination volume, not with seats. That is why this tab's composite outlier is not a software-multiple story. Watch inquiry volumes, mortgage origination, and any bureau or LLM-score narrative that claims substitution. The bureau file is not the FICO score.

summary: High-NA tools in the field are still a low-double-digit cumulative; N2 ramps are litho-limited later than the slide deck implied.
full_text: High-NA EUV cumulative shipments remain a low-double-digit installed base. That is enough for development layers, not enough to take the entire critical-layer load off Low-NA. N2 is not litho-unlimited; it is mix-and-recipe limited. The 2026–27 print is still Low-NA utilisation plus High-NA learning. China-insulation remains the structural support under the multiple. Chart is cumulative tools, not bookings.

summary: Epoch: capability-per-FLOP still ~3x per year from model and software; hardware is not the only cost-curve driver.
full_text: Epoch's latest cut still shows ~3x/year capability-per-FLOP from model/software (doubling ~7.6 months). That is the deepest non-hardware driver of the inference cost curve. It does not kill GPU demand in 2026; it changes the mix between training and serving, and it is why 'tokens per dollar' can fall while capex stays high. Primary source is the trends dashboard, not a vendor keynote.

summary: Hyperscaler AI-linked capex still guiding 20%+; the debate is duration of spend, not direction.
full_text: Four-co AI-linked capex is still being guided up. The incremental dollar is power, land, and networking as much as GPUs. Duration — 2027 and 2028 guides, not 2Q prints — is now the debate. A cut would show up first in delayed campus energisation dates and in HBM/CoWoS push-outs, not in a keynote. Funds-rate path is a second-order multiple input, not the demand input.

summary: EDA sign-off still sits in the agent's tool belt for chip design; that occupancy is not a seat-model rescue.
full_text: Agents writing RTL still call a verification/sign-off tool they cannot replace with a general model. That is why the two US EDA names score as callable surfaces on the vertical tab. It does not rescue a per-seat licence if the designer headcount falls; it does put them in the tool belt of every serious chip agent. Watch consumption-like term licences vs classic seats, and China export noise.

summary: Agent identity is a required primitive: authorise this agent to read customer records is a real API call.
full_text: Write the API call. 'Authorise this agent to read customer records' is Okta/SailPoint. 'Tell me which CVEs are on this host' is something the agent determines itself. Workforce seats can shrink; machine and agent identities multiply the base. That is the only clean P2 in pure cyber, and it still caps at 4. Watch non-human identity attach, Auth0 mix, and whether PANW/CyberArk crowds the same socket.

summary: Per-credit compute with no headcount assumption: agent querying converts mechanically into revenue.
full_text: Per-credit billing has no seat in the denominator. Agent querying, evals and retrieval over warehouse data convert directly. That is why this is the only P2-7 on the cyber-related tab. The risk is P3/P4: there is no licence shelter and FinOps programmes exist specifically to shrink this line item. Watch consumption growth vs RPO, and whether Iceberg/open table formats route work off-platform.

summary: Observability/evals is a named spoke; being the default is a 6, shipping an MCP server is not.
full_text: Evals and production tracing for agents is a spoke on the diagram. Default occupancy is what scores a 6; 'we shipped an MCP server' is not. LLM observability SKUs are attaching on the existing host-and-APM base. Watch product ARR mix, bit/log ingest growth, and whether traces from agent tool-calls actually land here vs in the hyperscaler console. Consumption is real; institutional shelter is not.

summary: SI benches are being re-badged as agent implementation; revenue-headcount decoupling is still the test.
full_text: Global SI decks now lead with agent implementation. The P1 test on this tab is whether revenue decouples from headcount. Most of the work is still people in, people out, with a model in the middle. A clean print would show utilisation up, hiring guides down, and IP/asset mix up. Watch ACN's booked AI pipeline vs actual delivery mix, and whether regional Israeli SIs (Matrix, One) see the same pull-through.

summary: 800G is the 2025 volume; 1.6T is the 2026 mix. In-rack copper still takes the short hop.
full_text: Datacenter optics TAM is a mix-shift, not a single number. 800G is the volume year; 1.6T is the 2026 ASP year. In-rack still wants copper (AEC/AEC) for the short hop; optics take the longer hop and the scale-out. Indium phosphide vs silicon photonics mix is the component read. Watch 1.6T qualification at the two US transceiver names and the CPO slideware vs actual shipments.

summary: Humanoid unit economics still negative below ~10k units; actuators and batteries set the floor, not the policy model.
full_text: Physical AI demos are not a P&L. At <10k units, humanoid BOM is dominated by actuators, reducers, and batteries. The policy model is the cheap part. Harmonic-drive-class reducers and vision sensors are the picks-and-shovels with actual gross margin. A 2026–27 pilot book is a traction print; it is not a software multiple. Chart: pilot units, not TAM slides.

summary: HBM controller IP is attaching into custom XPUs; this is a content-per-stack story, not a DRAM cycle.
full_text: HBM controller and chip-to-chip interconnect IP is landing in custom XPU tape-outs, not only in merchant GPUs. That is a content-per-stack print with a different cycle than commodity DRAM. Royalty and licence mix matters more than unit volume. Watch custom-silicon attach vs the merchant GPU customer concentration that still dominates the current print.

summary: Ontology as the semantic layer an agent needs to act on enterprise data; occupancy is real, default status is not.
full_text: The ontology pitch is the semantic layer an agent needs before it can write back into operational systems. That is a legitimate P1-6 claim on the horizontal tab, alongside the two cloud substrates. It is not yet the default. Watch remaining performance obligation, US commercial vs gov mix, and whether the bootcamp motion converts to consumption. AIP demos are not occupancy.

summary: Identity, authorisation, secrets and an immutable record are preconditions for agents; CVE-scan is the job the agent takes.
full_text: An autonomous actor needs an identity, scoped credentials, a data-reach policy, and an immutable record of what it did. Those are preconditions, not adjacencies. Vulnerability enumeration, alert triage and investigative link-analysis are the agent's job description. That split — not 'AI features shipped' — is the ranking on the pure-cyber tab. Varonis/Okta/SailPoint on one side; scanner/SOAR names on the other.

summary: Substrate and OSAT, not litho, are the 2026 advanced-packaging choke; HBM4 bits/wafer look fine.
full_text: Walk the packaging line, not the litho slide. CoWoS/SoIC-class capacity, ABF substrate and the OSAT stack are the 2026 choke. HBM4 bits per wafer are not. A foundry with CoWoS and a memory vendor with HBM both print this; a litho-only name does not. Secondary read is the US OSAT and substrate names, which are not on the close-watch tape. Chart lives on the CoWoS post.

summary: Custom XPUs plus merchant GPU: 2027 wafer mix is no longer a single-vendor story.
full_text: Marvell's custom XPU plus DSP/SerDes franchise is the other side of the Broadcom custom tape-out. 2027 advanced-packaging wafers are a two-vendor custom story plus merchant GPU, not a monopoly. The diligence is customer concentration (one hyperscaler can make the year) and whether the DSP/optics attach actually ships into the same rack. Design-win slides without CoWoS allocation are not a print.

summary: 18A yield and Intel Foundry external customers remain the diligence; a process name is not a wafer start.
full_text: 18A is a process name. Wafer starts, external foundry customers, and whether High-NA is actually in the critical-layer mix are the diligence. Internal GPU/accelerator attach can fill a line; it does not make a merchant foundry. Watch the IFS disclosure, not the node branding. ASML High-NA allocations to Intel are a necessary but not sufficient condition.

summary: AI-server attach is a systems print with thin incremental margin; the scarce parts sit upstream.
full_text: AI-server units are up. Incremental margin on the box is not. Liquid cooling, busbar and rack integration are real content; they are not HBM or CoWoS. The scarce print sits upstream at the GPU, switch, optical and memory names. Watch storage attach (power-constrained halls still need cheap capacity) and whether rack-scale liquid SKUs actually ship vs being quoted.

summary: Behind-the-meter power plus GPU hours is a cloud-adjacent print; it is not a software seat.
full_text: Behind-the-meter power plus a GPU-hour book is being sold as AI cloud. It screens as consumption (P2) without being a software company. Energisation dates, not hashprice, are the 2026 tell for the converted miners. Hut 8, IREN and Cipher are on the horizontal tab as cloud-adjacent, not as a crypto factor. Diligence is contracted GPU hours vs megawatts that are actually live.

summary: Reusable first stage is the 2027 P&L; this year's launch count is a cadence print, not the franchise.
full_text: Electron cadence is a 2025–26 cash print. Neutron and a reusable first stage are the 2027 P&L. Space is a theme with a small public tape: launch, antennas, and a handful of satellite-bus names. Government delay risk is the P3 analogue here. Chart: orbital launch counts, not TAM. Do not confuse a successful Electron with Neutron being de-risked.

summary: Direct-to-cell constellation still a coverage and capital story; constellation size is not revenue.
full_text: Direct-to-cell remains a coverage map plus a capital plan. Constellation size is not revenue; attach on the MNO side is. Spectrum, launch cadence and whether the phone-side SKU actually ships in volume are the 2026 tells. This is emerging tech with real physics and a long cash-need tail. Treat constellation photos as marketing, not as a subscriber print.

summary: Surgical robotics remains the cleanest physical-AI analogue with procedure data and a installed base; humanoids do not.
full_text: Intuitive still has the installed base, the procedure data, and the surgeon-liability wrapper that a humanoid pilot does not. That is why it scores as robotics/physical AI on the emerging tab while humanoid names do not. New platform cycles are a capex print for hospitals, not a software seat. Watch procedure growth and system ASP, not adjacent humanoid headlines.

summary: Agent 365 is an attempt to be the board the spokes sit on; occupancy of the orchestrator is the claim to test.
full_text: Copilot plus Agent 365 plus Entra is the claim to be the orchestrator rather than a spoke. That is a P1-7 if — and only if — real agent traffic is governed there. GitHub, Azure, and M365 distribution are the reasons the claim is plausible. Diligence is whether enterprises actually route tool-calls through that control plane or through a model console and a separate IdP. Watch Azure AI and security ARR mix, not demo counts.

summary: County systems of record still have multi-year, career-ending switching costs; AGI does not change the procurement cycle.
full_text: Court dockets, property assessments, permits, public-safety incidents: the record has legal force and the replacement cycle is measured in election terms. That is P3/P4 insulation, not a product launch. Vertical federal/gov names are the tab AGI damages least. Watch bookings vs RPO and whether payments attach actually shows up. Cognition is not the moat and never was.

summary: Digital-engineering benches are being asked for agent eval harnesses; that is still hours, not IP.
full_text: EPAM/Globant-class digital engineering is writing eval harnesses and retrieval pipelines as project work. It is hours. A productised IP mix would change the SI score; a slide deck does not. Watch utilisation, the hiring guide, and whether any reusable agent platform shows up as a disclosed offering vs T&M. Regional Israeli SI (Matrix, One) sees the same demand with a smaller, stickier local base.

summary: Edge vision SoCs remain a content story in physical AI; the model is the cheap layer.
full_text: Edge vision SoCs (auto, bodycam, robotics) are a units × content print. The on-device model is increasingly a download; the ISP, NPU and power envelope are not. This is a semis name with emerging-tech demand, not a software multiple. Watch design-wins in robotics/auto vs security-camera concentration, and whether a next-gen NPU actually attaches into a 2026–27 humanoid/AMR BOM.

summary: SSE/ZTna sits in the traffic path but is not invoked; inline inspection of agent calls is a 4, not a spoke.
full_text: Zscaler/Netskope-class SSE inspects the path. The orchestrator does not call them. That is P1-4: in the traffic path, not invoked. Consumption can still rise with agent calls through the proxy. It is not identity, it is not secrets, it is not the eval spoke. Watch billable users vs data/GB, and whether agent-to-SaaS traffic actually transits the proxy or goes out a dedicated egress the SSE never sees.

summary: Synopsys sign-off remains the other EDA callable surface; Ansys close is a multi-physics attach, not a seat rescue.
full_text: Sign-off, DRC and multi-physics are still invoked by any serious chip agent. The Ansys close (if/when fully digested) is a multi-physics attach onto that callable surface. It does not rescue a seat model if designer headcount falls, but it does widen the tool-belt. China licensing remains a real, discontinuous risk. Watch the mix of term vs perpetual and whether consumption language shows up in the K.

summary: Electron/Neutron aside, the public space tape is still antennas, buses and a handful of launch names.
full_text: Rocket Lab is the liquid US launch name that actually flies on a cadence. Neutron is the optionality. Iridium is the L-band utility with a real subscriber bill. ASTS is the direct-to-cell option. That is the close-watch space tape. Treat every other 'space AI' headline as a theme chip, not a ticker, until there is a filing.

summary: Now Assist sits on a plausible enterprise orchestrator; occupancy of ITSM as system of record is the surviving asset.
full_text: ITSM as the system of record for tickets, CMDB and workflow is real P5 state. Now Assist is the vendor wielding intelligence on top of that state. The orchestrator claim is plausible because the CMDB is where agent actions against enterprise services have to land. Diligence is whether those writes actually happen, vs Copilot/Agent 365 taking the board. Watch subscription remaining performance and AI product attach, not seat guides alone.
